properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 5 at 11:08AM EDT until October 5 at 1:15PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Apalachee Bay or Coastal Waters From Keaton Beach to Ochlockonee
River Fl out to 20 Nm...
Coastal Waters From  Ochlockonee River to Apalachicola FL out to 20
Nm...
Coastal waters from  Suwannee River to Keaton Beach out 20 NM...
Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 115 PM EDT.

* At 1108 AM EDT, severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from 21 nm
southwest of St. Marks to near K Tower to 45 nm south of S Tower,
moving northeast at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Buckeye Reef, O Tower, K Tower, S Tower, V Tower, Horseshoe Beach,
and Marker 24 Barge.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

officials for more details.

- Additional heavy rainfall will be possible through the morning
hours. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are expected
with locally higher amounts of up to 5 inches possible. This may
lead to flash flooding, especially in urban and poor drainage
areas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Additional rainfall totals of 2 to 4 inches are forecast for most
of the area with locally higher amounts of up to 6 inches
possible through Monday, especially along the Emerald and
Forgotten Coasts. Another area of concern is across south-central
Georgia where locally heavy rainfall since Friday afternoon has
primed the region more so than the rest of our area, so it wont
